newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian contracting firm goes private-sector.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian contracting firm goes private-sector.

text.p: General Upper Egypt Contracting Company shares went through the Egyptian stock exchange on Sunday after the state's National Company for Construction and Housing gave up its majority stake to private investors.
The Capital Market Authority daily report said 225,000 shares were registered at a price of 38.5 pounds ($11.34) each.
The holding company had originally offered investors at least 10 percent of the 300,000 shares in General Upper Egypt Contracting at a minimum price of 35 pounds per share.
The holding company also offered 10 percent of its stake in General Upper Egypt Contracting Company to the firm's Employee Shareholders Association.
General Upper Egypt forecast net after-tax profit for 1996/7 to rise to 2.15 million pounds from 2.027 million in 1995/6.
Net sales are expected to jump to 80 million pounds from 68.15 million in 1995/6.
The share offer was part of Egypt's privatisation-led economic reform programme.
